title: 3.4.2.2 Issue with starting a fresh Dash pod after the previous one failed
body:
S25 Ultra One UI Version 8.0 / Android 16

I recently had an issue where I started a pod and it failed. The pod had trouble inserting, caused bleeding and then sounded the permanent alarm tone. AAPS showed a java error. I wish I had taken a screenshot but it was a stacktrace to one of the java libraries. At this point, I broke the circuit and stopped the alarm.

This is when the real problems start. I discarded the problem pod through the UI. I then proceeded to prime and insert a new pod, and everything appeared to work properly. However when I go back to the pump status page it shows no pod connected. When I look in the history, there's no record of this pod at all even though I just activated and primed it!

For the third pod, I ended up discarding again and restarting my phone. At that point everything went smoothly. I think there is a problem with the state management for discarding after a failed pod.

One other thing that I feel like is important to mention is that during the priming and activation of the second pod, i got a notification saying "no pod active". I at first thought nothing of it since the pod had not yet been fully activated. But in hindsight, I think it was an indicator that the state changed and the new pod's configuration/initialization/logging had been lost.

One last thing. This bug actually happened to me before, when i first updated to 3.4.2.2. One significant difference was that in that scenario it happened after the update and wasn't the result of a failed pod. At the time I believed the problem was that I deleted and recreated my aaps directory. After that one incident, I hadn't had any problems for the past several weeks up until now. The reason I mention this is that I get the sense that the java error handling is not the problem here, and that it's a more simple state management/reset issue.

I think the bug, or part of it, is still there in 3.4.2.3. I use the Omnipod Eros, but I had the same problem that occurred with the Omnipod Dash. In my experience since the problem started, it seems to happen more frequently when the pod goes into error, either because the 80-hour limit or due to malfunctions. In that case, if I try to deactivate the pod, the process fails, and I’m always forced to use “Discard.” I think this is because AAPS tries to send other commands to the pod before the deactivation command, but since the pod is no longer responding, all the commands remain in the queue. This also happens when I press the “Discard” button: the Omnipod tab shows that there is no active pod, but the “Deactivate pod” command remains in the queue. To work around any issues, I close AAPS and clear the cache so that the command queue is cleared, but this shouldn’t be the app’s normal behavior.

@Ludovik95 no changes were made to the Eros driver. If the Eros has a similar issue, I would recommend creating a new issue for that.

In that new issue, you could refer to the commits 9d3bdce and 79e6f69; it’s likely that these are the changes that should be applied to the Eros driver as well in one way or another.

Too bad this was closed..... It just happened to me as well last night with 3.4.2.3 on Eros. Should I open a new report? I just uploaded logs and additional screenshots here for now...
I struggled throughout the night till 8AM, eventually uninstalled and went back to 3.3.1.3 which hasn't had issues. 

I've been running 3.4.2.3 (latest stable) for about 10 days on Samsung A52 5G (Android 12),
1) There was a problem with activating a pod (Emalink started flashing red in the middle of activation so I rebooted the link although right after that the pod started clicking and activating). We lost communications so I eventually had to press "discard". 

2) There was no active pod in the pod tab so I activated a new one (although Emalink started alternating red and green flashes as well during activation) but within 10 seconds of activation the pod was disabled by AAPS without asking me and I only heard  a faint beep after which it just showed "no active pod".
It seems that the deactivation for the prior pod was left in queue and it went through after the new one was activated?

3) Problem that I seemed to have overlooked the first time and I only saw now is that although there were no active pod in the pod tab, whenever I turned AAPS on it would show "trying to connect" in red at the bottom of the dashboard forever even though I never tried to activate a new one yet. In my opinion it seems that some queue is still holding onto some previous pod.

4) I tried every suggestion I could find to get rid of that connecting  message starting from every bluetooth suggestion I could find, I restarted the app and Emalink multiple times, I put the old pods away in the microwave, I cleared app cache, nothing worked.

5) I even cleared app data and restarted the app configuration from scratch but when reloading the saved settings obviously the presumed old pod was saved in those settings and it again started trying to connect 

6) Eventually I uninstalled and went back to the old trusty
@nlof the issue is closed as this is a *Dash* issue that has been fixed in 3.4.2.3. As I said before, if the Eros also has a problem please create a separate issue for that.
